scope.description: Three bluestone treads lifted, cleaned and set aside for reuse.
Reset the block core to level, full mortar bed.
Salvaged treads reset with a 2% wash, pointed in Type N.
One tread beyond salvage. New bluestone, matched thickness.

derivation.rationale: Low-middle: treads are accessible and undamaged.
Middle: level work, Type N pointing.

materials.spec: pre-1930 masonry — Portland will spall the face

totals.tax_note: Repair, not complete replacement — taxable on the full billed amount.

assumptions.why_it_matters: A fourth adds roughly $450 across reset and pointing.

tax_lines.basis: Partial replacement of an existing structure.

drivers: Whether the risers are sound underneath

swing: Whether the cracked tread is salvageable

explanation: Three treads come up, the core gets reset to level, and they go back down on a full bed with a wash so water runs off instead of sitting.
scope_sentence: Lift and salvage the existing bluestone treads, rebuild the step core to level on a full mortar bed, and reset the treads with a 2% wash, pointed in Type N.

objections.objection: Can you just re-point around the treads and leave them?
objections.response: They have settled out of level, so pointing seals the gap without fixing why it opened. It reopens in a freeze-thaw cycle.
objections.grounded_in: Rate card — 100+ freeze-thaw cycles a year, Monroe County

objections.objection: Why does one tread cost more than the others?
objections.response: That one is cracked through and cannot be reset. It is a new piece of bluestone matched to the existing thickness, not labour.

validity: Holds 30 days. Bluestone pricing is the one that moves.
tax_action: Add sales tax to the whole invoice — this is a repair, not a complete replacement.
